To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a stable inorganic acetylene, HBCN, was generated by thermally induced N _{2} elimination from a hydridoborane azide adduct in the presence of fluorinated triaryl boranes.

we have developed a new and potentially general strategy for the synthesis of a new class of donor-acceptor complexes of HBNH, which is the first such species of this elusive parent compound, by thermally induced elimination/1, 2-H migration from NHC⋅n-BH2N3 adducts.

a stable coordination complex of the inorganic iminborane HBNH was synthesized via a thermally induced N _{2} elimination/1, 2-H migration reaction from a hydrido(azido) borane adduct N H C⋅BH _{2} N _{3} (N H C=N-heterocycle carbene) in a fluorinated triarylboryl acceptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel synthetic strategies for the preparation and characterization of inorganic and organometallic compounds, with a particular emphasis on the use of N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) as ligands.
the development of new synthetic methods for the preparation of inorganic molecules with novel bonding patterns.
the development of new synthetic methodologies for the generation of inorganic compounds with unusual electronic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a new and modular route for the generation of unsaturated inorganic compounds, which is based on the elimination of a small, stable, and volatile molecule, N2, from a donor-acceptor adduct.
the reaction of the hydrido azido borane with the fluorinated aryl borane is a novel method of generating the elusive parent inorganics iminoboranes HBNH.
this work represents a new and promising approach to the synthesis of unsaturated inorganic compounds and their encapsulated derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elusive parent inorganinc iminoboranes, HBNH and its heavier congeners, have been encapsulated by a donor-acceptor interaction between a triarylborane and a NHC ligand.
we have been able to stabilize an elusive inorganic iminborane by using a NHC as an electron donor and an arylborane as an electron acceptor.
this is the first example of a stable, crystalline donor–acceptor complex of HBNH.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the parent inorganic imino group can be stabilized in the solid state by encapsulating it into a coordination cage formed by the interaction of the imino hydrogen and a boron center of a triarylborane.
a stable donor-accepton coordination complex of the parent inorganic imine HBNH can be prepared by a thermally induced N _{2} elimination from an adduct of HBNH and N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs).
the elusive parent inorganinc iminoboranes can be encapsulated by flanking coordinative interactions with a donor/acceptor ligand pair.
